newsitem.title: USA: Study urges U.S. privacy protection in digital age.
newsitem.headline: Study urges U.S. privacy protection in digital age.

text.p: A consortium of industry groups and privacy advocates urged the government Thursday to strengthen the laws designed to protect privacy in the new digital age.
The study was compiled by the Digital Privacy and Security Working Group representing computer, communications and public-inerest organizations.
It made the following findings and recommendations:
-- New technology is boosting the ability of law-enforcement officials to eavesdrop. As a result, "legal standards for government use of these new technologies must adequately protect privacy."
-- Standards should be strengthened covering government access to signaling information and other transactional data generated over the Internet or the phone system.
-- Laws barring scanning of wireless phone communications should be bolstered.

-- Proposals to change the law and make it easier for law-enforcement authorities to wiretap "must be scrutinized, and any amendments adopted must be narrowly crafted to ensure that they do not erode privacy protections."
